presentation_summary: 57-year-old man presented with three days of severe left-sided headache, facial pain, photophobia, neck stiffness, fever, nausea, vomiting, and dizziness.
He had multiple prior admissions over several years for similar presumed viral meningitis episodes that resolved after hospitalization.
Exam showed fever 38.5 C, neck stiffness, photophobia, no focal neurologic deficits, no skin lesions, and no genital ulcers.
CT head was normal; MRI was deferred because he remained neurologically stable and CSF PCR confirmed HSV-2.
Labs showed WBC 9.2 x10^9/L, CRP 12 mg/L, normal-range serum glucose, and CSF opening pressure 220 mmH2O.
CSF showed lymphocyte-predominant WBC 180/mm3, protein 0.65 g/L, and glucose 3.4 mmol/L; blood and CSF bacterial cultures had no growth.

CSF PCR was positive for HSV-2. Empiric IV acyclovir and chloramphenicol were started, antibiotics were stopped after negative bacterial cultures/PCR confirmation, and he transitioned to oral valacyclovir.
He improved over the next few days and was discharged with outpatient neurology follow-up; suppressive valacyclovir was discussed but deferred.

actual_treatment: intravenous chloramphenicol due to severe beta-lactam allergy while bacterial studies were pending
single dose dexamethasone for severe meningeal inflammation
oral valacyclovir 1000 mg three times daily for 14 days after HSV-2 confirmation

outcome.source_text_value: fever resolved, headache gradually improved, and he was discharged with outpatient neurology follow-up

The recurrent HSV-2/Mollaret context is encoded as context probability and risk_context, not as a separate disease name.
